source.title: BIRD: Behavior Induction via Representation-structure Distillation

record.file_problem: Whole paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The NLP experiment uses the weak-to-strong soft-label setup and PGR measure attributed to Burns et al., testing it on new datasets and student sizes. The vision experiments use a different, representation-structure transfer method.
record.gate_note: The NLP soft-label results and the vision transfer results are the study’s own tests. The paper also compares BIRD with other transfer methods; rows below retain the reported BIRD transfer results and the direct soft-label comparison relevant to the claim. Cited findings from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: Section 6 uses the Burns et al. setup: GPT2-Small soft labels train GPT2-Medium/Large on SciQ, BoolQ and Cosmos QA, reporting PGR. This bears on V1, V2 (BIRD loss added) and V3 (task and student size). The vision experiments are not weak-to-strong generalization in the claim's sense. The student trains on its own ground-truth labels plus a CKA loss to a robust teacher. PGR there is measured from the student's pre-transfer accuracy, not from a weak supervisor. So the vision results do not test V6 and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. In vision, the authors conclude that BIRD beats fine-tuning, LwF and Hints baselines for robustness transfer. They report it works from teachers up to 25x smaller, and that three teacher representation properties explain up to 85% of transfer variance. In NLP, which they call preliminary, BIRD sometimes complements soft-label weak-to-strong training, but not universally; neither method beats the weak teacher on BoolQ.
record.recipe_differences: The NLP experiment follows the weak-to-strong soft-label setup and uses PGR, adding BIRD representation-structure loss to the baseline. The main vision experiments transfer robustness by matching representation structure rather than training on weak-model labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by NLP dataset and student size. In vision, transfer depends on teacher representation properties, task/dataset, student capacity, and selected representation layer. The paper reports small layer deviations do not drastically reduce performance.

fits_no_version.finding: BIRD distils a small robust teacher's representation structure (CKA) into larger students trained on clean ground-truth data. This raises corrupted-data accuracy over the pre-transfer student, including for a ResNet152 student 25x larger than the teacher. PGR is measured from the student's pre-transfer accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-structure distillation from a small, robust teacher transfers OOD robustness to larger students on different datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher representation properties (probing accuracy, complementary knowledge, γ-robust usefulness) explain 73.6–85.5% of variance in robustness transfer. Very weak AlexNet teachers often fail.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher behavioral and task relevance predict success of representation-based behavior transfer.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says an implementation will be made public upon publication)
record.problems: NLP results are preliminary, cover only three datasets, and average three seeds; the reported per-seed results vary substantially. Vision transfer baselines with additional hyperparameters are reported at their best tuned performance. The vision experiments are not weak-label training, so they do not directly establish the weak-label claim.
record.rows_left_out: The 30 Table 5 entries are retained, but the separate Table 1 accuracy comparisons across three architectures and dataset pairs are omitted to stay within the row limit; their aggregate PGR values are recorded in r1–r3. Appendix B tables and figures with per-seed, clean-accuracy, and per-corruption breakdowns are also omitted; they are not needed to record the reported overall PGR and transfer outcomes. Appendix F per-seed NLP values are omitted because Table 2 reports the averages used here.

untested.parts: Only a GPT2-Small supervisor on three NLP QA tasks. Weak supervisor and ceiling accuracies are not reported.
Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors and bootstrapping are not tested. Only the BIRD CKA loss is added.
No supervisor-size sweep, no chess or reward modelling. No predictors of PGR in the weak-label NLP setting.
Not tested. The vision experiments transfer robustness via representation structure with ground-truth labels, not weak labels.

record.verdict_notes: Only Section 6/Table 2 (r34–r45) bears on the weak-to-strong claim. NLP results average three seeds, and Table 6 shows very large per-seed spread (e.g. Cosmos Medium soft-label 16.94–95.15; SciQ seeds include 0). Most V2 differences are within seed noise. The BIRD loss weight was tuned over five values while soft-label hyperparameters used repo defaults. Row r4's value contains a transcription error.

versions.untested_parts: Tests soft-label supervision from GPT2-Small on SciQ, BoolQ, and Cosmos QA with GPT2-Medium and GPT2-Large students; does not test other weak supervisors or tasks.
Tests adding BIRD representation-structure loss to soft-label training. Does not test auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or other loss variants.

Varies NLP task and student size, and analyzes teacher representation predictors in vision. Does not systematically sweep supervisor/student size in NLP; representation predictors are not analyzed for the NLP experiment.
The vision experiment evaluates held-out corruption types, but does not test the specified weak-supervisor failure modes or compare PGR under and without distribution shift in the weak-label setup.
No theoretical conditions requiring a student to beat its supervisor are established.
Tests robustness transfer in image classification only; other non-language modalities are not tested. The vision method transfers representation structure, not weak-model labels.
